```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE,
                     warning = TRUE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
```

The code below runs in a new R session with MIRA installed. The small
helper reads the metric-name map preserved on MIRA tables; keep its definition
when copying the later extraction examples.

```{r reader-tools}
library(MIRA)
metric_columns <- function(table, bases) {
  mapping <- attr(table, "mira_metric_names")
  actual <- bases
  mapped <- bases %in% names(mapping)
  actual[mapped] <- unname(mapping[bases[mapped]])
  stopifnot(all(actual %in% names(table)))
  actual
}
display_metrics <- function(table, fields, p_fields = character(0)) {
  display <- table[, metric_columns(table, fields), drop = FALSE]
  for (column in metric_columns(table, p_fields)) {
    display[[column]] <- format.pval(display[[column]], digits = 3,
                                   eps = 0.001)
  }
  display
}
```

## Scientific question and study design

This applied article assumes you can read a visit mean and a paired change
from [Getting started](frequentist-long-getting-started.html). It introduces
a group comparison while keeping the same follow-up-minus-baseline subtraction.
You will inspect estimates, intervals, denominators, and separate testing
families; the examples do not constitute a study-specific analysis plan.

Consider a synthetic glaucoma management study with intraocular pressure
(IOP) measured in mmHg. We compare two hypothetical pressure-lowering
strategies, A and B, at baseline, week 6 and week 12. These labels specify
simulated strategies, not medicines, doses or recommended treatment regimens.
The [National Eye Institute](https://www.nei.nih.gov/eye-health-information/eye-conditions-and-diseases/glaucoma/glaucoma-and-eye-pressure)
explains why pressure control matters in glaucoma, while emphasizing that
pressure tolerance differs between people. We do not specify a universal
target pressure or infer visual-field preservation from an IOP change.

Each of the 96 adults contributes one prespecified study eye. Its laterality
is assigned before the response values are generated, independently of
follow-up, and the fellow eye is not analyzed. The participant ID therefore
indexes independent people and their one selected eye. A real protocol must
define selection before inspecting outcomes. Treating both eyes as independent
or setting `strict_id = FALSE` would not solve bilateral correlation.

A visit-specific difference compares observed group pressures at that visit.
A difference in change compares follow-up-minus-baseline pressure changes.
A global time-by-strategy interaction concerns all modeled visits. Separate
within-group significance tests do not establish a between-group difference.

The simulation allocates 48 adults to each strategy. Shared participant
variation and visit-specific measurement noise induce imperfect repeated
measurements. Strategy B is assigned a larger average reduction by construction.
All readings represent a fictional standardized tonometry schedule and one
measurement protocol; the simulation is not calibrated to a glaucoma treatment trial.

```{r two-arm-data}
set.seed(441021)
n <- 96L
allocation <- sample(rep(c("Strategy A", "Strategy B"), each = n / 2L))
selected_eye <- sample(c("Right", "Left"), n, replace = TRUE)
strategy_b <- allocation == "Strategy B"
person_pressure <- rnorm(n, 0, 2.6)
glaucoma <- data.frame(
  participant_id = sprintf("G%03d", seq_len(n)),
  study_eye = selected_eye,
  treatment_arm = allocation,
  iop_t0 = 26.5 + person_pressure + rnorm(n, 0, 1.1),
  iop_t1 = 24.5 + person_pressure - 1.0 * strategy_b + rnorm(n, 0, 1.3),
  iop_t2 = 23.5 + person_pressure - 2.2 * strategy_b + rnorm(n, 0, 1.5)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(glaucoma$participant_id),
          !anyNA(glaucoma$participant_id),
          all(is.finite(as.matrix(glaucoma[c("iop_t0", "iop_t1", "iop_t2")]))),
          all(as.matrix(glaucoma[c("iop_t0", "iop_t1", "iop_t2")]) > 0))
table(glaucoma$treatment_arm)
head(glaucoma, 4)
```

## Specify the groups and reference explicitly

The first ordered visit is baseline. Explicit source variables and labels
make that decision auditable. `reference_arm` sets the first group in the
comparison and model order; it does not adjust for baseline. With
`analyses = NULL`, the individual module switches below apply. Turning off
models keeps the initial comparison lightweight. Core paired changes and
the complete-profile Friedman branch still run.

```{r two-arm-analysis}
group_fit <- mira_info_long(
  glaucoma, id = "participant_id", outcomes = "iop",
  time_vars = c("iop_t0", "iop_t1", "iop_t2"),
  time_labels = c("Baseline", "Week 6", "Week 12"),
  arm = "treatment_arm", reference_arm = "Strategy A",
  covariates = character(0), arm_tests = TRUE,
  alpha = 0.05, p_adjust_method = "holm",
  improvement_direction = "lower", stable_threshold = 1,
  plots = TRUE, model = FALSE, outliers = FALSE, correlations = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)
stopifnot(inherits(group_fit, "mira_info_long"),
          isTRUE(group_fit$arm_analysis$enabled),
          identical(group_fit$arm_analysis$levels[[1L]], "Strategy A"))
group_fit$settings[c("reference_arm", "confidence_level", "p_adjust_method")]
```

`alpha = 0.05` requests 95% confidence intervals; it does not define clinical
response. Here `stable_threshold = 1` calls observed changes within the closed
interval [-1, 1] mmHg stable. This is a teaching rule, not a validated minimum
important difference, measurement-repeatability limit or target-pressure rule.
With `improvement_direction = "lower"`, the software calls larger reductions
"Improved" in this pressure-lowering context. This label does not establish
that every lower pressure is safe or that glaucoma progression was prevented.
Neither setting removes observations.

Declaring `outcomes = "iop"` prefixes metric names with `iop_`, while
structural fields such as `arm`, `n`, and `time_label` retain their names.
The helper above resolves each table's documented `mira_metric_names`
attribute instead of guessing its metric column spelling.

## Start with estimates and uncertainty

Group-specific means and intervals describe IOP among study eyes of participants
observed at each visit. These intervals concern a group mean, not the spread
of individual observations or an individual's prognosis.

```{r arm-descriptives}
arm_desc <- group_fit$arm_analysis$descriptives
knitr::kable(arm_desc[, metric_columns(arm_desc, c(
  "arm", "time_label", "n", "mean", "sd", "ci_lower", "ci_upper"
))], digits = 2, col.names = c("Arm", "Visit", "n", "Mean", "SD", "Lower", "Upper"),
caption = "IOP (mmHg) by assigned strategy and visit, with pointwise 95% mean intervals.")
```

Participants with an unavailable group do not enter these group summaries;
each visit otherwise uses its finite pressure values. Within-group changes require
both baseline and that follow-up for the same participant. This complete
teaching dataset has 48 participants per group at every visit and in each
change comparison. In incomplete data, those denominators can differ even
within one group.

Within-group baseline changes describe a different quantity. Positive
follow-up-minus-baseline values mean increased IOP; negative values mean
reduced IOP in mmHg. A group-specific interval describes that group's mean change.
Comparing whether two such intervals separately exclude zero is not a valid
test of the difference between groups.

```{r arm-changes}
arm_change <- group_fit$arm_analysis$change_descriptives
knitr::kable(arm_change[, metric_columns(arm_change, c(
  "arm", "to_label", "n", "mean_change", "ci_lower", "ci_upper"
))], digits = 2, col.names = c("Arm", "Visit", "n", "Change", "Lower", "Upper"),
caption = "Paired IOP change (mmHg) from baseline within each strategy.")
knitr::kable(arm_change[, metric_columns(arm_change, c(
  "arm", "to_label", "improved_n", "stable_n", "worsened_n"
))], col.names = c("Arm", "Visit", "Improved", "Stable", "Worsened"),
caption = "Software change categories under the illustrative 1-mmHg threshold; these are not clinical target achievements.")
```

## Distinguish visit differences from differences in change

The tables use `arm_b - arm_a`. A negative Strategy-B-minus-Strategy-A
difference denotes lower pressure under B in this simulated context. Welch tests allow
unequal variances and assume independent participants between groups.
Their confidence intervals are pointwise, not simultaneous intervals
adjusted to match the multiplicity-adjusted p-values. Hedges' g is a
small-sample-corrected standardized difference using pooled variability;
it complements the original mmHg estimate.

```{r between-arm-results}
at_visit <- group_fit$arm_analysis$time_pairwise
in_change <- group_fit$arm_analysis$change_pairwise
knitr::kable(at_visit[, metric_columns(at_visit, c(
  "time_label", "n_a", "n_b", "mean_difference_b_minus_a",
  "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "hedges_g"
))], digits = 3,
col.names = c("Visit", "n (A)", "n (B)", "Difference", "Lower", "Upper", "g"),
caption = "Visit IOP differences (mmHg): Strategy B minus Strategy A.")
knitr::kable(display_metrics(at_visit, c(
  "time_label", "welch_t_p", "welch_t_p_adj", "wilcoxon_p_adj"
), p_fields = c("welch_t_p", "welch_t_p_adj", "wilcoxon_p_adj")),
col.names = c("Visit", "Welch p", "Holm Welch p", "Holm rank p"),
caption = "Visit-specific inference; Welch and rank tests have separate adjustment families.")
knitr::kable(display_metrics(in_change, c(
  "to_label", "n_a", "n_b", "difference_in_change_b_minus_a",
  "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "welch_t_p_adj"
), p_fields = "welch_t_p_adj"), digits = 3,
col.names = c("Visit", "n (A)", "n (B)", "Difference", "Lower", "Upper", "Holm p"),
caption = "Differences in baseline IOP change (mmHg): Strategy B minus Strategy A.")
```

Display copies format small p-values as `<0.001`; the numeric values in the
analysis object remain available for calculation. To verify the direction and
interval independently, select the final visit and the named group pair,
then reconstruct its means and Welch interval from the original values,
sample variances, Welch degrees of freedom and t quantile. This uses no MIRA
helper or t-test result field and confirms the contributing participant counts.
It does not validate the scientific design or extend inference beyond its
sampling and variance assumptions.

```{r verify-final-contrasts}
final_visit <- at_visit[at_visit$time == "iop_t2" &
  at_visit$arm_a == "Strategy A" & at_visit$arm_b == "Strategy B", ,
  drop = FALSE]
final_change <- in_change[in_change$from == "iop_t0" & in_change$to == "iop_t2" &
  in_change$arm_a == "Strategy A" & in_change$arm_b == "Strategy B", ,
  drop = FALSE]
group_a <- glaucoma$iop_t2[glaucoma$treatment_arm == "Strategy A"]
group_b <- glaucoma$iop_t2[glaucoma$treatment_arm == "Strategy B"]
delta <- glaucoma$iop_t2 - glaucoma$iop_t0
change_a <- delta[glaucoma$treatment_arm == "Strategy A"]
change_b <- delta[glaucoma$treatment_arm == "Strategy B"]
welch_interval <- function(b, a) {
  variance_b <- var(b) / length(b)
  variance_a <- var(a) / length(a)
  degrees_freedom <- (variance_a + variance_b)^2 /
    (variance_a^2 / (length(a) - 1) + variance_b^2 / (length(b) - 1))
  mean(b) - mean(a) + c(-1, 1) * qt(0.975, degrees_freedom) *
    sqrt(variance_a + variance_b)
}
welch_visit_ci <- welch_interval(group_b, group_a)
welch_change_ci <- welch_interval(change_b, change_a)
stopifnot(nrow(final_visit) == 1L, nrow(final_change) == 1L,
  final_visit$n_a == length(group_a), final_visit$n_b == length(group_b),
  final_change$n_a == length(change_a),
  final_change$n_b == length(change_b),
  isTRUE(all.equal(final_visit[[metric_columns(final_visit,
    "mean_difference_b_minus_a")]], mean(group_b) - mean(group_a))),
  isTRUE(all.equal(unname(unlist(final_visit[, metric_columns(final_visit,
    c("ci_lower", "ci_upper")), drop = FALSE])),
    welch_visit_ci)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(final_change[[metric_columns(final_change,
    "difference_in_change_b_minus_a")]],
    mean(change_b) - mean(change_a))),
  isTRUE(all.equal(unname(unlist(final_change[, metric_columns(final_change,
    c("ci_lower", "ci_upper")), drop = FALSE])),
    welch_change_ci)))
```

MIRA also returns omnibus Welch and Kruskal--Wallis tests at each visit
(`time_omnibus`) and for each baseline change (`change_omnibus`), and
asymptotic unpaired Wilcoxon tests in the pairwise tables. Rank-based tests
concern distributional/rank differences; without additional assumptions,
they are not simply tests of means or medians. Selecting the smallest
p-value across methods after seeing results is not a defensible plan.

`baseline_balance` is the first-visit subset of the pairwise comparisons.
In a randomized study, baseline p-values do not diagnose the success of
randomization or select adjustment variables. Inspect estimated imbalances
and report the allocation process. In an observational study, balance on
measured variables does not rule out confounding.

```{r baseline-balance}
balance <- group_fit$arm_analysis$baseline_balance
knitr::kable(balance[, metric_columns(balance, c(
  "time_label", "mean_difference_b_minus_a", "ci_lower", "ci_upper"
))], digits = 2, col.names = c("Visit", "Difference", "Lower", "Upper"),
caption = "Exploratory baseline IOP difference (mmHg): Strategy B minus Strategy A.")
```

## Understand the adjustment family

Holm's method controls family-wise error under arbitrary dependence. MIRA
adjusts the finite Welch p-values across all visit-by-pair rows in
`time_pairwise` as one family. Change comparisons form a separate family.
The Wilcoxon families, omnibus families, and missingness tests are also
separate: visit-specific Welch omnibus p-values form one family, visit-specific
Kruskal--Wallis p-values another, and each has a separate IOP-change family.
The missingness family spans visits. The core all-participant paired t and
signed-rank comparisons each have their own visit-pair family; Friedman
post-hoc and model contrasts add further families documented in the advanced
tutorial. No correction across this entire collection is implied. This
verification reproduces the adjustment from the stored raw values.

```{r verify-adjustment}
raw_p <- at_visit[[metric_columns(at_visit, "welch_t_p")]]
adjusted_p <- at_visit[[metric_columns(at_visit, "welch_t_p_adj")]]
finite <- is.finite(raw_p)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(adjusted_p[finite],
                          p.adjust(raw_p[finite], method = "holm"))))
```

Bonferroni also controls family-wise error, but its rule differs from Holm.
Benjamini--Hochberg (`"BH"`) targets the false discovery rate under independence
or appropriate positive dependence of true-null p-values;
Benjamini--Yekutieli (`"BY"`) permits arbitrary dependence, provided the
individual null p-values are valid, at a cost in power. Prespecify the scientific family and error
criterion. `p_adjust_method = "none"` does not address multiplicity. An
adjusted p-value is neither an effect size nor the probability a null
hypothesis is true.

```{r arm-plots, fig.cap="Observed IOP means (mmHg) and pointwise 95% mean confidence intervals for one study eye from each of 48 adults per strategy at baseline, week 6 and week 12. Symbols and line types distinguish strategies without color. These intervals do not quantify uncertainty in the difference between strategies."}
stopifnot(inherits(group_fit$plots$arm_mean_ci, "ggplot"))
print(group_fit$plots$arm_mean_ci + ggplot2::labs(x = "Scheduled visit", y = "IOP (mmHg)"))
```

`arm_change_ci` visualizes group-specific changes and `arm_difference_ci`
visualizes between-strategy IOP differences when available. Inspect
`names(group_fit$plots)` for the plots actually created.

## Predict the sign after changing the reference

Before running the code, predict what changes when Strategy B becomes
the reference. The underlying people, visits, and IOP values stay fixed.
The same comparison is now Strategy-A-minus-Strategy-B: its estimate
changes sign and its interval endpoints reverse; the two-sided p-value
does not change. This is an orientation check, not a new scientific analysis.

```{r reference-checkpoint}
reversed_fit <- mira_info_long(
  glaucoma, id = "participant_id", outcomes = "iop",
  time_vars = group_fit$time_vars, time_labels = group_fit$time_labels,
  arm = "treatment_arm", reference_arm = "Strategy B",
  covariates = character(0), arm_tests = TRUE,
  alpha = 0.05, p_adjust_method = "holm",
  improvement_direction = "lower", stable_threshold = 1,
  plots = TRUE, model = FALSE, outliers = FALSE, correlations = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)
reversed_table <- reversed_fit$arm_analysis$change_pairwise
reversed_endpoint <- reversed_table[
  reversed_table$from == "iop_t0" & reversed_table$to == "iop_t2" &
  reversed_table$arm_a == "Strategy B" &
  reversed_table$arm_b == "Strategy A", , drop = FALSE]
estimate_field <- metric_columns(final_change, "difference_in_change_b_minus_a")
reverse_field <- metric_columns(reversed_endpoint, "difference_in_change_b_minus_a")
stopifnot(nrow(reversed_endpoint) == 1L,
  isTRUE(all.equal(final_change[[estimate_field]], -reversed_endpoint[[reverse_field]])),
  isTRUE(all.equal(final_change[[metric_columns(final_change, "welch_t_p")]],
    reversed_endpoint[[metric_columns(reversed_endpoint, "welch_t_p")]])),
  isTRUE(all.equal(final_change[[metric_columns(final_change, "ci_lower")]],
    -reversed_endpoint[[metric_columns(reversed_endpoint, "ci_upper")]])),
  isTRUE(all.equal(final_change[[metric_columns(final_change, "ci_upper")]],
    -reversed_endpoint[[metric_columns(reversed_endpoint, "ci_lower")]])))
orientation <- data.frame(
  subtraction = c("Strategy B - Strategy A", "Strategy A - Strategy B"),
  difference_in_change = c(final_change[[estimate_field]], reversed_endpoint[[reverse_field]])
)
knitr::kable(orientation, digits = 3,
  caption = "The same final IOP-change comparison (mmHg) in the two reference orientations.")
```

## Extend to three groups

We now generate a separate cohort with 108 adults and three hypothetical
pressure-lowering strategies. Each contributes one prespecified eye. Units,
three-visit schedule and later-minus-baseline subtraction are retained; the
new feature is a third strategy and therefore three group pairs per visit.
These are not additional measurements from the original 96 people.

```{r multi-arm-study}
set.seed(441022)
n3 <- 108L
arm3 <- sample(rep(c("Strategy A", "Strategy B", "Strategy C"), each = n3 / 3L))
eye3 <- sample(c("Right", "Left"), n3, replace = TRUE)
subject3 <- rnorm(n3, 0, 2.8)
extra_reduction <- c("Strategy A" = 0, "Strategy B" = 2.4, "Strategy C" = 1.3)[arm3]
glaucoma_three <- data.frame(
  participant_id = sprintf("H%03d", seq_len(n3)), study_eye = eye3, arm = arm3,
  iop_t0 = 27 + subject3 + rnorm(n3, 0, 1.2),
  iop_t1 = 24.8 + subject3 - extra_reduction / 2 + rnorm(n3, 0, 1.4),
  iop_t2 = 23.8 + subject3 - extra_reduction + rnorm(n3, 0, 1.5)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(glaucoma_three$participant_id),
  all(as.matrix(glaucoma_three[c("iop_t0", "iop_t1", "iop_t2")]) > 0))
three_fit <- mira_info_long(
  glaucoma_three, id = "participant_id", outcomes = "iop", arm = "arm",
  time_vars = c("iop_t0", "iop_t1", "iop_t2"),
  time_labels = c("Baseline", "Week 6", "Week 12"),
  reference_arm = "Strategy A", covariates = character(0),
  analyses = "arm_tests", improvement_direction = "lower",
  stable_threshold = 1, p_adjust_method = "holm", verbose = FALSE
)
omnibus <- three_fit$arm_analysis$time_omnibus
knitr::kable(display_metrics(omnibus, c(
  "time_label", "n", "n_arms", "welch_anova_p", "welch_anova_p_adj",
  "kruskal_p", "kruskal_p_adj"
), p_fields = c("welch_anova_p", "welch_anova_p_adj", "kruskal_p", "kruskal_p_adj")),
row.names = FALSE,
col.names = c("Visit", "n", "Strategies", "Welch p", "Holm Welch p", "Rank p", "Holm rank p"),
caption = "Three-strategy IOP omnibus comparisons at each visit.")
stopifnot(nrow(three_fit$arm_analysis$time_pairwise) == 3L * choose(3L, 2L))
```

With more than two groups, the reference is first in the level order but
comparisons also include pairs that do not contain the reference. Retain both
group names when selecting or displaying any comparison. At the final visit,
the sign of each estimate follows the printed `Arm B - Arm A` ordering.

```{r three-arm-pairs}
three_pairs <- three_fit$arm_analysis$time_pairwise
final_pairs <- three_pairs[three_pairs$time == "iop_t2", , drop = FALSE]
knitr::kable(display_metrics(final_pairs, c(
  "arm_a", "arm_b", "n_a", "n_b", "mean_difference_b_minus_a",
  "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "welch_t_p_adj"
), p_fields = "welch_t_p_adj"), digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
col.names = c("Arm A", "Arm B", "n A", "n B", "B - A", "Lower", "Upper", "Holm p"),
caption = "Final-visit IOP differences (mmHg) and pointwise 95% intervals; Holm adjusts all nine visit-by-pair tests.")
```

The Welch omnibus hypothesis asks whether all group mean pressures are equal at a
visit. It does not identify which groups differ. The pairwise tables answer
those separate questions with their own adjustment family. The same
interpretation boundaries apply to change-score tests.

`analyses` replaces all five module switches when supplied: omitting
`"arm_tests"` disables between-arm work even when an arm is resolved. The
arm can still be carried in trajectories and long-format output.

```{r disable-arm-tests}
ungrouped <- mira_info_long(
  glaucoma_three, id = "participant_id", outcomes = "iop", arm = "arm",
  covariates = character(0), analyses = "none", verbose = FALSE
)
stopifnot(!ungrouped$arm_analysis$enabled,
          is.null(ungrouped$arm_analysis$time_pairwise),
          "arm" %in% names(ungrouped$long_data))
```

## From exploratory differences to an analysis plan

Consider mmHg estimates and intervals alongside a prespecified
clinically meaningful magnitude and the study design. Statistical
significance alone establishes neither clinical importance nor causation.
These unadjusted comparisons do not control for covariates; baseline pressure-change
values are not automatically equivalent to baseline-adjusted follow-up
models. A treatment-by-time model provides a distinct global question and
covariate-adjusted contrasts.

Continue with [missing data](frequentist-long-missing-data.html) before
interpreting incomplete follow-up. See
[advanced models](frequentist-long-advanced-models.html) for formulas,
interaction hypotheses, and diagnostics, and
[reporting](frequentist-long-reporting.html) to preserve an analysis bundle.
